preamble: The shift from the postalveolar fricative [ʃ] to the velar fricative [x] is a case of backing: the place of articulation moves from the postalveolar region back to the velum, with loss of sibilance. The textbook case is Spanish, where in the 16th and early 17th centuries prepalatal /ʃ/ (spelled ⟨x⟩) was retracted to velar /x/ (respelled ⟨j⟩), in both northern and southern Peninsular Spanish.

examples.note: Prepalatal /ʃ/ was moved back to velar /x/ and lost its sibilance; the spelling changed from ⟨x⟩ to ⟨j⟩.

examples.from: Old Spanish dixo /ˈdi.ʃo/ 'he said' (< Latin dīxit)
